notes: August 2026 cycle, REFRESHED to the 2026-08-02 seam (training through 2026-08-01); the split artifact was rebuilt for that window (all four producer checks pass, shredder-drift trailing edge 0.0000% against the new production raw pull) while the paid curve below was deliberately carried forward UNCHANGED so the refresh delta isolates fresher data. Replaces the `m` marketing-lift bidirectional overlay for mobile with a MEASURED paid/organic split (adjustment code `p`). Fenix training rows are multiplied by organic_share(date, country) measured from the client-level growth_source mirror, the model forecasts organic only, and paid is stacked back on: measured paid for training rows (so they stay byte-identical to raw actuals) and marketing's paid LEVEL (lift + anchor 922,250.47) allocated by trailing-28d Fenix DAU share for forecast rows. Paid then contributes exactly its own value with no Prophet interaction, unlike `m`, whose bidirectional overlay absorbed 58% of any change to the curve. KEY ASSUMPTION: the measured share only exists from 2024-06-01 (mozdata.fenix.active_users retains a rolling ~25 months), but mobile DAU trains from 2020-12-31, so the earliest measured per-country share is HELD FLAT backwards over ~3.5 years. At 2024-06-01 paid was 1.10% of Fenix DAU ex-IR, so that assumption is bounded at ~1.1pp; see _index.md. IR is excluded from the split (98.8% organic, and marketing's curve is explicitly ex-IR), which also honours the `scope.exclude_countries` key that the `m` code path silently ignored. Non-Fenix apps are treated as 100% organic - Firefox iOS carries no paid signal at all (paid_vs_organic_gclid 100% NULL, Adjust attribution collapsed Sept 2024, 0 paid-attributed clients in 2026-07) and no campaigns run for Focus. Marketing's curve ends 2026-12-31 and is HELD FLAT through forecast_end_date rather than zero-filled, which would drop ~1.56M on 2027-01-01. Mutually exclusive with `m`: main.py raises if both specs claim the same applies_to_forecast_start. ALLOCATION KEY CHANGED vs `m`: marketing's national paid level is allocated by each country's share of MEASURED PAID DAU over the trailing 28 days (`trailing_paid_dau_share`), not by share of total Fenix DAU (`trailing_dau_share`, what `m` used). Paid intensity ranges from 0.2% of Fenix DAU in RU to 27.6% in ID, so a total-DAU key pushes paid into markets with essentially none and starves the campaign markets; it also makes the geographic mix jump at the seam. `trailing_dau_share` remains supported so the difference stays measurable.
